title: Tool Use and Function Calling
description: Designing tools that models call correctly, safely and efficiently.

questions.prompt: What makes a tool description effective for a model?

options.text: A one-word name only
A clear name, a description of when to use it and well-documented parameters
Hiding the parameters so the model guesses
Very long descriptions copied from the source code

questions.explanation: The model chooses tools from their names and descriptions. Say what it does, when to use it, and what each parameter means.

questions.prompt: Who actually executes a function the model "calls"?

options.text: The model itself, inside its weights
The user's browser automatically
Nobody; the call is only illustrative
Your application code, which then returns the result to the model

questions.explanation: The model emits a structured request. Your code runs the function and sends the result back as an observation.

questions.prompt: A tool returns a 50,000-line log file. What is the best practice?

options.text: Return a concise, relevant summary or a filtered slice, with a way to fetch more
Return all of it so nothing is lost
Return nothing
Return it as an image

questions.explanation: Tool output consumes context. Return what is useful and let the agent request more detail if needed.

questions.prompt: Why validate tool arguments before executing them?

options.text: Models never make mistakes, so it is unnecessary
Validation is only needed for read-only tools
Arguments can be malformed or unsafe, and validation prevents bad or dangerous actions
It makes the model faster

questions.explanation: Treat model-produced arguments like user input: check types, ranges and permissions before acting.

questions.prompt: What should a tool return when it fails?

options.text: An empty string
Crash the whole agent
A clear error message the model can understand and act on
A fake success so the loop continues

questions.explanation: Informative errors let the agent retry with corrected input or choose another approach. Silent or fake success leads to wrong conclusions.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of a standard such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

options.text: It gives a common way to expose tools and data to many different AI applications
It replaces the need for an LLM
It makes models run offline
It is a prompt template format

questions.explanation: A shared protocol means a tool integration can be written once and used by any compatible client, instead of bespoke glue per app.
